newsitem.title: USA: Marathon sets Garyville propylene venture.
newsitem.headline: Marathon sets Garyville propylene venture.

text.p: Marathon Oil Co said it intends to develop grassroots polymer grade propylene and polypropylene facilities at its Garyville, La., refinery with privately owned Epsilon Products Co.
The project is subject to execution of definitive agreements, the USX Corp subsidiary said.
The project involves construction of purification facilities which are expected to produce 800 million pounds per year of polymer grade propylene from a current refinery feedstock stream.
It includes an 800 million pounds-per-year Unipol polypropylene facility similar to that operated by Epsilon in Marcus Hook, Pa.
Preliminary project engineering is underway, with plant start-up slated for 1999, Marathon said.
The companies credited the project to a mutual desire to fulfill expected demand growth in polypropylene moving into the year 2000.
Marathon has been operating the Garyville refinery since 1976, marketing a portion of its refinery grade propylene in the merchant market.
Epsilon has been in the polypropylene business since the start-up of its first plant in 1991 and has just completed its second plant in Marcus Hook, Pa.
"This project should improve the value of a refinery by-product over its use as a fuel component, and establishes the Garyville facility as a base chemical feedstock supplier," Marathon said.
